title: MergeProducts rescales recipes_pos amounts that are stored in their own unit (only_check_single_unit_in_stock = 1)

labels.name: php
labels.description: Pull requests that update php code

body:
Found while validating PR #921 (#901), 2026-10-13. Reproduced by the validator against master code. This is a pre-existing arithmetic defect.

`StockService::MergeProducts` multiplies every `recipes_pos.amount` of the removed product by `factor`, the removed product's stock unit converted to the kept product's. For rows with `only_check_single_unit_in_stock = 1`, the amount is stored in the row's own unit `qu_id`, not the stock unit. The views read it that way (`db/pgsql/baseline/05_views_l3.sql` ~:164, :174; `RecipesService.php` ~:56-66). Rescaling those rows changes the quantity they mean.

## Example (validator probe)

B (removed) is stocked in tablets and A (kept) in packs. B has tablet→pack 0.1 and box→tablet 30. A has box→pack 3. B has a flag=1 recipe row of "1 box", with 1 kcal per tablet for B and 10 kcal per pack for A. #921's conflict check passes (30 × 0.1 = 3), and the merge goes through.

After the merge the row reads "0.1 box", and its calories in `recipes_pos_resolved` drop from 30 to 3. Costs and the shopping-list conversion shrink by the same factor.

## Done when

- [ ] MergeProducts does not rescale flag=1 `recipes_pos.amount`. Flag=0 rows, which are stock-unit amounts, keep the rescale.
- [ ] A regression test asserts calories, costs and the shopping-list quantity for a flag=1 row are unchanged across a merge with equal effective factors.

Related: #901, #921, ADR-0036.
